note: Purge Queues adds three @PurgeQueue plugins to the Purge module: database_alt (table purge_queue_alt, extra type/expression columns), database_unique (dedups via a pre-SELECT findItem on type+expression), database_unique_upsert (table purge_queue_upsert, primary key = sha256(type:expression), dedups via SQL UPSERT). No admin UI of its own (configure=null), no permissions, no config schema, no Drush. The active queue is chosen through Purge's own selection at admin/config/development/performance/purge and stored in config purge.plugins:queue; read/write it via \Drupal::service('purge.queue')->getPluginsEnabled()/setPluginsEnabled([...]) (default 'database'). Medium/hard cases are grounded in that live selection: introspection reads which queue is active; execution switches the active queue to one of this module's plugins, verified against the live purge.queue service. Scripts restore the shipped default (database) as baseline.

evals.prompt: The purge_queues module is installed alongside Purge. What problem does it solve and which queue plugins does it add?
evals.expected_output: purge_queues adds extra Purge queue backends that stop the queue filling with duplicate invalidation items. It provides database_alt ('Database (extended)', adds type/expression columns), database_unique ('Database unique', rejects duplicate type+expression items), and database_unique_upsert ('Database unique (upsert)', dedups via an UPSERT keyed on a hash of type:expression for better performance).

evals.prompt: With purge_queues installed, how do I actually make my Purge site use the deduplicating 'Database unique' queue, and where is that choice stored?
evals.expected_output: purge_queues has no settings page of its own; you select the queue through Purge at Configuration > Development > Performance > Purge (admin/config/development/performance/purge), choosing 'Database unique' or 'Database unique (upsert)'. The choice is stored in Purge config purge.plugins:queue; programmatically use \Drupal::service('purge.queue')->setPluginsEnabled(['database_unique']).

evals.prompt: How does the purge_queues 'database_unique_upsert' queue avoid duplicate items, and what is different about its database table compared with the standard database queue?
evals.expected_output: database_unique_upsert uses a SHA-256 hash of the invalidation's type:expression as the row primary key (table purge_queue_upsert) and inserts with an SQL UPSERT, so re-queuing the same invalidation just overwrites the existing row instead of adding a duplicate. Because the primary key is a string hash (not an int), it overrides claimItem/selectPage etc.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the running Purge configuration and tell me which purge queue plugin is currently active.
evals.expected_output: The active queue is database_unique: purge.plugins:queue is 'database_unique' (readable via \Drupal::service('purge.queue')->getPluginsEnabled()).

evals.prompt: Inspect this site's live Purge setup and state which queue engine is selected. Is it one of the purge_queues deduplicating queues?
evals.expected_output: The selected queue is database_unique_upsert (the upsert-based deduplicating queue from purge_queues): purge.plugins:queue is 'database_unique_upsert'.

evals.prompt: This site's Purge module is currently using the standard core 'database' queue. Using the purge_queues module, switch the active Purge queue to the deduplicating 'Database unique' queue (database_unique) and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The active Purge queue becomes database_unique (purge.plugins:queue = 'database_unique'), e.g. via \Drupal::service('purge.queue')->setPluginsEnabled(['database_unique']).

evals.prompt: My cache-invalidation queue keeps piling up with duplicate entries and I want the fastest deduplicating option that purge_queues offers. It's currently on the normal database queue. Switch it to the upsert-based unique queue and make it live.
evals.expected_output: The active Purge queue becomes database_unique_upsert (purge.plugins:queue = 'database_unique_upsert').
